To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the developed methodology can provide an efficient and effective tool for the CD of obstacles to air navigation.

the proposed methodology allows to: 1. identify the areas where the obstacle risk is potentially changed in the airport perimeter, 2. detect and locate the obstacles to air navigations potentially changed within the airport perimeter.
a new methodology to detect obstacles in pairs of high spatial resolution ortho-rectiﬁed multi-spectral satellite imagery is presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a CD strategy based on the analysis of multi-temporal HR satellite images.
the development of a methodology based on the analysis of HR multi-spectral satellite imagery for the detection of changes in a large geographical area.

the development of a CD methodology for the detection of changes in the periphery of the airports, and in particular of changes in the height of obstacles to air navigation, through a comparison of HR satellite images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach allows to identify and locate the most relevant CD areas, which can be subsequently analyzed in detail with more expensive very HR data or/and detailed on-the-field surveys.
the proposed approach is a valid and effective methodology for CD and for the assessment of changes potentially associated with obstacles to air navigation.
the proposed methodology is a promising and innovative solution for the identification of changes associated to potential variations of obstacles to air navigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed CD strategy is based on the use of the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), which is the most common vegetation index used to monitor the state of vegetation.

the proposed methodology is based on the use of the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), the normalized difference bareness index (NDBI), and a new index named the normalized difference building index (NDBIm) to extract the vegetation, the bare soil, and the built-up areas, respectively.

the CD strategy is based on the comparison between the two images of the same area at different times and the analysis of the resulting change map in order to identify the areas with the highest probability to contain changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed approach allows to detect and locate changes with a high accuracy, and to identify their nature (i.e., natural or artificial) with a good level of confidence.
the proposed methodology is able to detect changes in the terrain surface with a high accuracy and a good reliability.

a simple and fast CD technique, based on the comparison between pairs of HR ortho-rectiﬁed satellite images, can be used as a pre-screening tool for the detection of potentially relevant changes in wide areas.
